**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

I swept the agreement for most-favoured-nation language — "no less favourable"/"no less favorable", "most favored nation", "more favorable", "at least as favorable", "comparable terms", "match" — and found no hits anywhere in the document.

I then read the two planner-flagged sections in full:

- **Article IX (FINANCIAL PROVISIONS)** — upfront payment, capped milestones ($520M aggregate), tiered ex-US royalty rates, royalty reductions/Royalty Floor, U.S. profit/loss share, payment terms, taxes, records and audit. All economics are fixed and negotiated; nothing keys Sanofi's pricing or payments to terms granted to any third party.
- **Article VII (MANUFACTURING AND SUPPLY)** — Section 7.3 sets supply pricing by a specified formula ("The price charged by the manufacturing Party under any Supply Agreement shall be equal to [***]"), not by reference to third-party terms.

Sanofi has no obligation to offer RevMed terms no less favourable than those given to others, and no obligation to match third-party offers. That satisfies the preferred position (no MFN obligation on Customer), so there is nothing to redline. Worth noting for completeness: there is also no Vendor-granted MFN in our favour — that would be welcome under the playbook but its absence is not a deviation under this rule.
